en: Udāna 3.1 Kammavipākajasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now on that occasion a certain bhikkhu was sitting not far from the Blessed One,
having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and experienced intense, sharp, harsh, and bitter suffering born of the ripening of past kamma.
Enduring that feeling, mindful and clearly comprehending,
he was not distressed. The Blessed One saw that monk sitting not far away, having folded his legs crosswise and set his body erect,
enduring a painful, sharp, harsh, and bitter sensation born from the ripening of past karma— enduring it mindfully, clearly comprehending, and undistressed.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“For the bhikkhu who has abandoned all karma,
shaking off the dust of deeds done in the past;”
For one who is without "mine," established as such,
there is no purpose in conversing with people. Thus ends the first [verse].
